items.title: Birding Apps Bring More People Into the Wild
items.content: <article>On Bloomberg This Weekend, writer and photographer Alexandra Marvar explains how apps such as Merlin are making birding easier and more accessible, helping draw new people to a hobby that offers an escape into nature. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Marvar also explores whether technology can remove some of the challenge, learning and satisfaction that traditionally come with identifying birds.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Mexico Stresses Sovereignty in US Cooperation
items.content: <article>Mexico’s foreign minister Roberto Velasco Álvarez tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the country maintains a strong relationship with the US while insisting cooperation on security must respect Mexico’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, he says Mexico remains cautiously optimistic about ongoing trade negotiations as it seeks relief from US tariffs on automobiles and steel. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Russia Ukraine War Becomes Economic Battle
items.content: <article>New York Times Kyiv bureau chief Andrew Kramer tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Russia and Ukraine are increasingly targeting each other’s economies as the war shifts toward attacks on energy, transportation and export infrastructure. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kramer says Ukraine is using its expanding drone arsenal to target Russia’s oil industry and its ability to finance a prolonged war. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: McDonald’s Sell-Off Hits 30% as Big Mac Inflation Spurs Pushback
items.author: Peyton Forte
items.content: <article>McDonald’s Corp. faces a key challenge as it fights to reinvigorate a sagging stock price: Winning back the cost-conscious diners who believe its menu has become too expensive.</article>

items.title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
items.content: <article>Campus Moms, smuggling butter, bringing iced coffee to a job interview, and the 'what's for dinner' question: Join Alexis Christoforous, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Higher Bond Yields Mark a Return to Normal
items.content: <article>Ritholtz Wealth Management founder Barry Ritholtz tells Bloomberg This Weekend that rising bond yields reflect both a normalization of interest rates and inflationary pressures from factors including tariffs and higher energy prices. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Ritholtz says higher yields have made fixed income more attractive while investors should consider whether strong equity gains have pushed their portfolios away from their intended allocations. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Northeast Faces Wind, Rain and Coastal Flooding
items.content: <article>Bloomberg News meteorologist Craig Allen tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the nor'easter will bring waves of heavy rain and strong winds to the Northeast, along with risks from falling trees, localized flooding and dangerous coastal conditions. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Allen says coastal flooding could affect Long Island, the Jersey Shore, Connecticut and Massachusetts as rough ocean conditions persist through multiple high-tide cycles. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Iran War Endgame Remains Elusive
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Mideast geoeconomics lead Dina Esfandiary tells Bloomberg This Weekend that a protracted Iran war, marked by cycles of escalation and pauses in fighting, is a key scenario as deep divisions over the Strait of Hormuz complicate diplomacy. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Esfandiary says Gulf Arab states are pressing to avoid further escalation as they seek to limit the economic and security damage from the conflict.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: The China Trade Problem That Tariffs Alone Can't Fix
items.content: <article>China ran a $1.2 trillion trade surplus last year, many of its companies don't need to make a profit, and its exports are growing at two to three times the rate of the global economy. Michael Froman, former US Trade Representative under President Obama and now president of the Council on Foreign Relations, tells us why Xi Jinping sees a consumer-led economy as a political threat, and what happens when China finally runs out of countries willing to buy. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Trump Xi Summit Leaves Big Issues Unresolved
items.content: <article>Bloomberg North Asia correspondent Stephen Engle tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping bought more time to negotiate over trade while major disagreements involving Taiwan, Iran and technology remain. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Engle explains how competition over AI and unresolved economic and security issues are shaping the next phase of US-China relations. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: US Says China to Buy 10 Million Tons of Coal in 2027, 2028
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>China agreed to import at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the US next year and again in 2028, according to the White House, in a sign of further progress in easing trade frictions between the world’s two largest economies.</article>

items.title: Billionaire Charoen’s Asset World Targets $1 Billion REIT IPO
items.author: Anuchit Nguyen
items.content: <article>Asset World Corp Pcl’s new Thai Real Estate Investment Trust aims to raise at least $1 billion through a listing as it seeks funds to expand its hotel and commercial property business, according to a senior executive.</article>

items.title: Blackstone Cements Shift From Star Dealmakers With Baratta Exit
items.author: Preeti Singh and Dawn Lim
items.content: <article>If there was any doubt that Jon Gray is now the center of gravity at Blackstone Inc., the past few weeks have erased it.</article>

items.title: Wall Street Week | China’s Trade Reckoning, Syracuse’s Second Chance, Humanoids in Healthcare
items.content: <article>This week, Council on Foreign Relations President Michael Froman breaks down China's export machine, why twenty years of US pressure hasn't worked, and what happens next. And, can a $100 billion Micron factory transform Syracuse from a Rust Belt cautionary tale into a potential model for American reindustrialization? Plus, a bridge named for a hockey legend was meant to strengthen the supply chain between the US and Canada, but the neighbors can’t agree on their trade relationship. Later, with 760,000 care aide openings expected every year in the US and a $400 billion long-term care bill, humanoid robots are an early bet on technology filling the care gap. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Ellison Pledges $9.2 Billion More in Oracle Shares for Loans
items.author: Christopher Palmeri and Brody Ford
items.content: <article>Larry Ellison, a key figure behind Paramount Skydance Corp.’s deal to buy Warner Bros. Discovery Inc., has pledged 67 million more shares of Oracle Corp. as collateral for personal loans than he had at the same time last year.</article>

items.title: Search for the Next Leader of the UN
items.content: <article>UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres' term ends this year, and three Security Council straw polls have provided no consensus. Guyana’s Permanent Representative to the UN Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett is one of the top contenders. She speaks to Bloomberg Businessweek Daily about why she wants the job, and how she views the UN's role in the world moving forward. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Keeneland CEO on Annual Yearling Sale
items.content: <article>Shannon Arvin says Keeneland’s yearling sale is running ahead of last year’s pace and is on track to top $550 million, making it the largest horse sale in the world. She said the auction is already up 3% to 4% this year after increasing by 24% last year, reflecting strong demand and continued interest in horse racing. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Jev, an AI Model That Can’t Chat, Takes On Bigger Rivals
items.content: <article>Jev, an AI model built by a former OpenAI researcher, went viral over the past week with the promise of a cheaper and faster alternative to large language models. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: SK Hynix’s Solidigm Is Said to Weigh US IPO as Soon as 2027
items.author: Bailey Lipschultz
items.content: <article>SK Hynix Inc.’s Solidigm is considering a US initial public offering as soon as next year, according to people familiar with the matter.</article>

items.title: David Booth on Investing, Dimensional and Staying Calm | The David Rubenstein Show
items.content: <article>David Booth started Dimensional Fund Advisors out of a Brooklyn brownstone in 1981 with an idea that challenged conventional investing: investors should have exposure to smaller companies as part of a diversified portfolio. Today, Dimensional manages more than $1 trillion. Booth sits down with David Rubenstein to discuss his new book, "Stay Calm," which applies his investment philosophy of staying calm during periods of market volatility, to navigating the uncertainties of life. He's on this week's episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This interview was recorded August 10 in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>
